description: What holding a browser for that long would cost, without holding one. `maxCost` is the whole window at the per-minute rate. It is a ceiling, not a bill, because the minutes you do not use come back when the session closes.

proxy.description: Where the session leaves from, fixed for its whole life. Defaults to the managed residential pool.

city.description: A city inside `country`, by name: `curitiba`, `new york`. Managed pool only. Most calls leave from that city and a few from elsewhere in its state, as the pool's own location data places them. A place with nobody in it right now answers `PROXY_REFUSED` at no charge; ask for the state or the country alone.

country.description: Where the call should look like it comes from, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (`us`, `br`). Name one and the managed pool leaves from that country. Leave it out and the page sees a US browser, from an address we pick. A scrape or a map on the managed pool makes one exception: a site whose address ends in `.br`, `.de`, `.es`, `.fr`, `.it`, `.jp`, `.nl`, `.pl` or `.uk` is read from its own country. The browser's clock and languages follow the country on every pool.

pool.description: Which exit to leave through. "residential" is the managed pool, metered by the megabyte; "custom" is your own proxy, free on every plan, bytes never billed.

server.description: Your own proxy, `http(s)://[user:pass@]host:port`. Required for pool "custom", refused for the managed one.

state.description: A state or region inside `country`, by name: `california`, `são paulo`. Managed pool only. Spell the name out, since an abbreviation like `sp` finds nobody. In the US and Brazil the browser's clock follows the state.

timeoutMin.description: How long to hold the browser, in minutes. Credits for the whole window are reserved when the session starts and the unused minutes are handed back when it closes, so asking for longer than you need costs nothing extra. Defaults to 10; your plan sets the ceiling.
